_readme: Cards pulled on camera, one entry per hit, keyed by YouTube video id.
SOURCE is the My Hits tab of the workbook. It used to be a comma separated
list crammed into one Video Log cell, which broke on the first typo and the
first stray comma: 'Phantasmal Falmes' made a misspelled SET read as a card
name, and a comma where a dash belonged split one hit into two. Both are
corrected by hand in scripts and recorded, not guessed silently.
Prices are NOT stored here. They are looked up at build time from
public/data/cards/*.json and data/psa10.json, so a price refresh moves the
rip pages without re-importing the sheet and one card can never show two
different numbers on two different pages.
PROMOS CARRY set:null AND A number. The two Black Star Promos from the Mega
Charizard X UPC were first resolved against Phantasmal Flames and matched SET
cards of the same name, which put the wrong Oricorio ex on the page and lost
the Mega Charizard X ex entirely. Promos are not in the 23 sets we price, so
they resolve against public/data/printings instead: that gives a real scan and
no price, which is the truth. MEP #023 and #024 are adjacent, as one product's
promos usually are; a second Mega Charizard X ex exists at #029.
PROMO PRICES ARE STORED, unlike every other price on the site, and the reason
is that nothing can regenerate them. TCGdex carries no TCGplayer pricing for
promo sets, so a promo has no price in the nightly feed at all. These two came
from pricecharting.com, read in a browser on 2026-08-13, and each entry keeps
its own priceSource, priceAsOf and priceUrl so the page can say where the
number came from and when. They will go stale; that is the trade for having
them, and the date on the page is what makes it honest.
The $38.75 confirms MEP #023 over #029: the url the owner supplied ends -23.
forSet, on a promo only: which set page it appears on. A promo is in no
set, so without this it either appears on every set page the video
touched, which put two cards at the top of four pages, or on none. The
answer that reads true is the set it shipped alongside. A promo with no
forSet is named at build time and shown on no set page, rather than
guessed onto one. It still appears on its rip page and the Hall of Fame.
THIS FILE IS REBUILT PER VIDEO NOW, NOT ADDED TO. scripts/import-sheet.mjs
could only ever add or update a row, so every mistake its Hit Info parser
had ever made was permanent and every FIX to that parser made a page worse:
the corrected name arrived and the wrong one stayed beside it. The Costco
UPC rip reached 21 cards for 14 real hits and the six-box First Partner rip
7 for 3, three generations of parser output stacked on one page. A video
whose Hit Info cell was read is rebuilt from that cell, and every row it
drops is printed. A row carrying ANY field the parser does not write is
another source's row: the whole My Hits tab, both promos above, anything
hand-added. Those are read and never written, because on them an ABSENT
field is somebody's answer. That is what keeps `set` off the two promos.
printing: what the owner wrote before the colon, kept verbatim beside the card
rather than glued onto its name. "First Partner Illustration Collection
(Series 1) Alola Region Promo : Rowlet, Litten, Popplio" is three cards
sharing one promo pack, and prepending the context published three card
names no catalogue has ever held. It is the words he typed to say WHICH
Rowlet, and it is here so they are not lost. The three resolve to MEP 043,
044 and 045, which data/first-partner.json confirms are the Series 1 Alola
promos.
"NOTHING DERIVES ANYTHING FROM THIS FIELD" WAS TRUE HERE UNTIL 21 AUGUST
2026 AND IS NOT NOW. shared/first-partner.mjs reads `printing` as the key
that joins these rows to data/first-partner.json, which is where their
numbers and prices already were: /first-partner-illustration-collection
.html had been publishing a raw price and a PSA 10 for all three since 19
August while their six rows on M7NqqhR8V4M and xNGxOuMpSiw printed "No
market price". They are on /hall.html now as well. The join is on this
field and NOT on the card name, because a bare "Rowlet" on some other rip
is a different card; see that module for the rest of the reasoning.

TCGplayer's market figure is $10.24 and is recorded here as context rather than as a published price, because it is one marketplace where the site's figure is a guide value across several. ALREADY IN THE BINDER since 16 September, added from a photograph of the cards he pulled that day. The two records are different things and both are right: data/30th-binder.json is what he owns, this is what came out of a rip on camera. Hand kept until the My Hits tab carries it.

The 30th prints Hisuian Zorua TWICE -- 122/128 Common and 145/128 Illustration Rare -- with identical card text, HP 60 and Scratch (20), so nothing readable separates them and the rarity is the only thing that can choose. One gold star IS the Illustration Rare symbol, so this is 145. "Gole" is a typo for Gold and not a fourth kind of star. NOT the Zorua at 095, which is the ordinary Kantonian one and a different Pokemon. CORROBORATED INDEPENDENTLY OF TODAY'S MESSAGE: data/30th-binder.json has held Hisuian Zorua 145 since 16 September, entered off a close-up photograph of three cards together, and its note reaches the same printing by the same symbol. Same physical card, video released six days later, which is the pattern every 30th rip has followed -- he opened these around the 16th and is publishing them one a day. Nothing is added to the binder here. HIS TITLE SAYS "NEW Moonbreon Card?!" AND THAT IS NOT THE HIT. Moonbreon is the hobby's name for the Umbreon VMAX alt art out of Evolving Skies; the 30th does print Umbreon ex, in the Battle Deck and the night Ultra Premium Collection. The title is his own question about the set rather than a second card out of this pack, and the hit is what he typed. NO PRICE YET: PriceCharting holds no row for 145, so the card renders without one rather than borrowing the Common's. Written "Illustration Rare" with a capital R to match this set's own checklist casing. Hand kept until the My Hits tab carries it.

The owner, 22 September 2026: "you can also add for a hit from the 30th Celebration set card 099 Black Star Promo Greninja ex". The second card out of the same rip -- the promo that comes in the 30th Celebration Greninja ex Tin, alongside the Hisuian Zorua pulled from its Pack #1. THE NUMBER 099 BELONGS TO A DIFFERENT CARD IN THIS SET AND THAT NEARLY SHIPPED. A Black Star Promo is numbered in its own run, so this 099 is not the main set's 099, which is HYDREIGON. The 30th page's hits band matched a hit to the checklist ON THE NUMBER ALONE, so adding this row rendered a Greninja ex wearing Hydreigon's scan and Hydreigon's price. The band requires the NAME to agree as well now, and this row correctly matches nothing: it is a promo and the 199 card checklist does not contain it. The two Greninja ex that ARE in the set, 021 Double Rare and 148 Special Illustration Rare, are different cards and neither is this one. NO PRICE, AND NONE IS BORROWED. PriceCharting carries no row for this promo -- searched 22 September 2026 and its Greninja results are the XY and Mega Greninja promos, nothing numbered 099 -- which is what a six day old card looks like. The card publishes its name and nothing else rather than inheriting a figure from a card that merely shares a number. ALREADY IN THE BINDER as a promo since 16 September, with its number corrected from a photo-derived 035 to the typed 099 on the 21st. Promos sit outside the 199 there and this row does not change that.
